summary: Kastelorizo Airport (KZS/LGKJ) is a tiny airport serving the remote Greek island of Kastelorizo (Megisti), the easternmost inhabited island of the Dodecanese archipelago, located just 2 km off the Turkish coast. With its very short runway suitable only for small turboprop aircraft, the airport provides a vital but weather-dependent air link to this isolated community of roughly 500 residents. The island gained wider recognition following the 1991 Academy Award-winning film 'Mediterraneo' set during World War II.
faqs:
Q: How long is the runway at Kastelorizo Airport?
A: The runway is very short, approximately 800 meters, which limits operations to small turboprop aircraft such as the Dornier 228 typically used by Olympic Air.

Q: Are flights to Kastelorizo frequently cancelled?
A: Yes, flights are often cancelled due to strong winds common in the eastern Aegean, especially during winter months. Travelers should build flexibility into their itineraries.

Q: Which airlines fly to Kastelorizo?
A: Olympic Air operates scheduled flights connecting Kastelorizo with Rhodes, which serves as the main hub for onward connections to Athens and other Greek islands.

Q: Can I fly directly to Kastelorizo from Athens?
A: There are no direct flights from Athens. Travelers must connect through Rhodes (RHO), with the short hop taking approximately 25 minutes.
transport_tips: The airport is located just outside the main village of Megisti, roughly a 15-minute walk downhill to the harbor where most accommodations and tavernas are situated. There are no public buses or taxis waiting at the airport, so arranging pickup with your hotel in advance is highly recommended. If walking, carry minimal luggage as the downhill path can be steep and uneven in places.
local_tip: Book the earliest flight of the day if possible—afternoon winds frequently build up and can delay or cancel later flights, especially outside the calm summer months.
